svg.title: Bit Manipulation: Kernighan Clear, Two's Complement Isolate, SWAR Popcount & Gosper's Hack
svg.desc: Animated 4-quadrant Word-RAM bit manipulation reference showing Brian Kernighan's x & (x - 1) lowest-bit clear, x & -x lowest-bit isolation, 32-bit SWAR parallel popcount tree reduction, and Gosper's Hack NEXT-COMBINATION(x) mask progression.
svg.text: Bit Manipulation on Word-RAM: Kernighan, Two's Complement, SWAR & Gosper
Exact O(1) word-level identities, O(log w) branchless popcount, and combinatoric bitmask enumeration
Why It Clears Exactly Bit p (Module 02 §10)
Subtracting 1 flips bits 0..p (lowest 1 becomes 0; trailing 0s become 1).
Submask loop: for (s = mask; s > 0; s = (s - 1) & mask) → O(3^n)
JS uint32 guard: coerce x >>> 0 when bit 31 may be set!
2. Isolate Lowest Set Bit: x & (-x) via Two's Complement
Adding +1 to ~x carries through the trailing 1s (0..p-1), stops at p (setting it to 1),
and leaves bits > p complemented. ANDing x with -x cancels all bits except bit p.
Used in Fenwick / Binary Indexed Trees: i += (i & -i) and i -= (i & -i).

g.text: Top byte = b3 + b2 + b1 + b0; unsigned >>> 24 avoids sign extension

svg.text: Invariant after step s: every 2^s-bit field holds popcount of its input bits.
r ^ x captures changed run (4 ones); dividing by c shifts down & drops 2 bits.
Strict Increasing Order for k = 3, n = 5:
• Math.clz32(-1) === 0 (uint32 view) • 64-bit masks need BigInt.asUintN(64, x)
